reviewSummary: The act itself is sound and correctly bounded. The warrant (D-314 item 8 / Q4) reproduces verbatim from live COORD and was introduced by the commit the draft cites; the D-293 Decision 6 C4 three-limb order and Decision 8 reservation likewise reproduce verbatim. Every frozen artifact digest matches, every recited field (v9's leftoverDesign partition, file08StatusToken, and all four OBL-RESERVED-TABLES fields; v5-of-G22's partition; both CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED / binds NOTHING recitals) is byte-exact, and both file 08 owner cells are quoted distinctly without collapse. Custody, wording, identifier and boundary audits are all clean: no deictic, no unstemmed version token, no invented selector value or identifier, no partition change, no SATISFIED or QUALIFIED claim, no C4-c or C4-d limb, no v10, file 08 untouched. One defect blocks: the draft twice attaches D-294 Decision 1 to the three frozen owner-reservation sentences, and D-294 Decision 1's own bytes do not reach them - its predicate requires a sentence in a recorded leftover-join that names another lineage's leftover-join version and asserts currency, and none of the three sentences satisfies any of those elements, while two sit in a contract and an occupancy rather than a join. D-294 Decision 5 additionally states the entry 'does not decide any reserved number, list, owner, or Class A question' - the owner question is the one this citation is being used to settle. The citation is also superfluous: the frozen sentences say choosing the owner is a separate decision, and the draft's own next sentence ('This COORD entry is that separate decision') is the correct and sufficient reading. A second, lesser defect: the draft's definite phrase 'The three frozen sentences' undercounts against its own disjunctive predicate, which four frozen sites satisfy.

mustFix.class: governing-rule citation contradicted by the cited rule's own bytes
mustFix.site: Subject paragraph, two sentences: 'The three frozen sentences that say choosing the packet's owner is a separate decision, or that the join does not choose that packet's owner, remain custody at D-125, D-219, and D-268 under D-294 Decision 1.' and 'platform-tcb leftover-join.v9 `$.proposedLaterWork[2]` cites that the join does not choose that packet's owner; under D-294 Decision 1 that citation is custody at D-268.'
mustFix.defect: D-294 Decision 1 does not reach any of the three sentences. Its predicate, quoted from live COORD, is conjunctive: the sentence must (i) sit 'In a recorded leftover-join', (ii) name 'another lineage's leftover-join version (dotted or spaced spelling, stem immediately before `leftover-join`)', and (iii) 'assert currency' in the enumerated vocabulary (remains/remain/is/are [the] current; the inverted form; 'Cite X leftover-join.vN as the current ...'; or 'still measure(s)'). None of the three cited sentences satisfies (ii) or (iii) - none names any leftover-join version and none asserts currency. Two also fail (i): platform-tcb-contract.v45 `$.platformProfile.populationPacket` sits in a contract and harness.DR-G22.platform-abi-loader.v2 `$.filesystems.laterAct` sits in an occupancy, neither of which is a recorded leftover-join. Only v9 `$.proposedLaterWork[2]` is in a join at all, and it fails (ii) and (iii).
mustFix.aggravation: D-294 Decision 5 confines the entry: 'This entry governs the reading of cross-lineage citation currency from this heading forward', and expressly 'does not decide any reserved number, list, owner, or Class A question.' The draft uses Decision 1 to fix the standing of owner-reservation sentences - precisely the owner question D-294 disclaims. No adopted entry has ever cited 'D-294 Decision 1' (zero occurrences in live COORD); the nearest recorded discipline runs the other way, D-303 recording 'Does not treat D-294 as the warrant.'
mustFix.internalTension: The two clauses also work against the entry's own warrant. If the owner-reservation sentences are custody at their recording headings and not standing claims, then the draft's next sentence - 'This COORD entry is that separate decision' - has nothing standing to answer. The draft needs those sentences live as a forward-pointing invitation; D-294 Decision 1 would read them as spent.
mustFix.whyItBlocks: A permanent COORD entry would record a governing-rule application the rule's bytes contradict, extending a narrowly drafted cross-lineage currency-reading rule to arbitrary disclaimers in contracts and occupancies. That is precedent a later reader relies on.
mustFix.loadBearing: The operative content does not depend on it. D-314 item 8 is the warrant and the frozen sentences invite exactly this act; the repair removes a false citation without touching the assignment.
mustFix.repair: Delete both 'under D-294 Decision 1' clauses. The accurate basis is already in the draft: the three sentences are frozen bytes at D-125, D-219 and D-268 that this act does not rewrite, and each says choosing the packet's owner is a separate decision, which this COORD entry is. If a custody rule is wanted, cite one whose predicate these sentences actually meet.

shouldFix.defect: The draft's predicate is disjunctive and four frozen sites satisfy it, not three: platform-tcb-contract.v45 `$.platformProfile.populationPacket` ('Choosing its owner is a separate decision.'); harness.DR-G22.platform-abi-loader.v2 `$.filesystems.laterAct` ('Choosing its owner is a separate decision.'); harness.DR-G22.platform-abi-loader.v2 `$.proposedLaterWork[4]` ('Choosing that packet's owner is a separate decision.'); and platform-tcb-leftover-join.v9 `$.proposedLaterWork[2]` ('... does not choose that packet's owner.'). The definite article plus the 1:1 mapping onto D-125, D-219 and D-268 omits the occupancy's second site.
shouldFix.provenance: The count of three matches DECISION-PACKETS/C-plan/C4-dr126-tcb-owner-grammar-profiles.md section 4.1, which states 'the record says three times that `Choosing its owner is a separate decision.`' and enumerates the same three paths. shouldFix.repair: Say 'four', or drop the numeral ('The frozen sentences that say ...'), or enumerate the three intended paths explicitly as the C-plan does.

observations: The draft's no-cell-edit branch sentence reads 'D-170 through D-235 and D-237 through D-340. D-272 is CONTESTED and is not on that no-cell-edit adoption branch', which on its face places D-272 inside the stated span while excluding it. This is not charged: it is the adopted house form, carried verbatim by at least twelve prior entries including D-340 ('D-237 through D-339. D-272 is CONTESTED and is not on that branch'), and the draft's added word 'adoption' makes the intended sense - the adoption branch, not the numeric span - marginally clearer than the precedent. The endpoint correctly advances to D-340 and the span does not reach D-236.

The draft takes the COORD-only shape and declines the C-plan's optional companion join (C4-dr126-tcb-owner-grammar-profiles.md section 4.1: 'Optional companion: platform-tcb-leftover-join.v10'). That is the correct election under this dispatch, which forbids recording v10, and it keeps the act to the single limb D-293 sequenced first.

Readiness effect and Reversibility reproduce the COORD-only precedent at D-310 and D-311 verbatim ('Total only before a later dependent leftover rewrite, SATISFIED cycle, or file-08 cell rewrite'), with the overturn code correctly advanced to C-D341. The 'Does not unwrite' list names D-125, D-219, D-268, D-271, D-293, D-294, D-314 and D-340 - every heading the entry leans on.
